note: MACHINE-READABLE P5 PITCH-GATES. Eitan's decision 2026-08-02: gates bind BOTH loops — this session AND the away loop that ships to main. Until now a gate was prose in EXCAVA_END_PLAN.md that a session had to notice and choose to honour, which is exactly how the Router gate got built straight through on 2026-08-01. A gate listed here with verdict:null BLOCKS the work it names. Only Eitan sets a verdict. standing_checks prints every open gate at the top of every fire, so a loop cannot claim it did not know.
law: PROTOCOLS.md P5 — autonomy with three pitch-gates: an OVERHAUL, a NEW TOOL, or DEEPER ACCESS is Eitan's call, never the loop's.

gates.blocks: Adding langgraph or crewai (or any heavy orchestration framework) to requirements.txt.
gates.question: END PLAN §2 says the 5 classes sit 'on LangGraph/CrewAI'. Neither is installed; requirements.txt has 4 deps and the runtime is GitHub Actions + Eitan's PC. Adopt the framework, or build on the existing excava_bus?
gates.claude_recommendation: Build on the existing bus (Ponytail: reuse before building). A heavy orchestration dep on every CI run is real cost with no demonstrated need.
gates.note: The away loop built Router in its fire 95 WITHOUT this gate being answered — it composed excava_agents/excava_engines and added NO dependency, which happens to match the recommendation. Outcome fine, governance not: a gate was bypassed because nothing enforced it. That bypass is why this file now exists. Recorded honestly rather than quietly closed.

gates.claude_recommendation: Keep as a standing rule, not a gate.
